matters.title:
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby recognize Darcia Ashley-Amber Reed for her extraordinary vigilance, compassion, and unwavering advocacy; and, 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Tuesday, August 4, 2026 to be “Darcia Ashley-Amber Reed Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..body
WHEREAS, on September 3, 2025, Darcia Ashley-Amber Reed received an urgent call from her lifelong friend of more than 35 years, Tara Yilmaz, reporting that her sister, Marla James, had failed to report to work and could not be reached. Recognizing the urgency of the situation, Darcia immediately left work, traveled to Marla's residence, and confirmed that Marla's vehicle remained at the home, heightening concern for her safety; and,

WHEREAS, upon the arrival of Marla's mother, Darcia demonstrated exceptional composure, and leadership by coordinating with first responders and steadfastly advocating for an immediate welfare check. Understanding that every moment could mean the difference between life and death, she urged emergency personnel to enter the residence without delay, ensuring the situation received the urgent response it required; and,

WHEREAS, first responders Lt. Mike Sulida, Matt Murrman, Mike Welch, and Ryan Bichler responded swiftly and professionally to the emergency, entered the residence, and discovered Marla unconscious inside the home. Through their prompt assessment, decisive actions, and commitment to protecting life, they were able to secure immediate medical intervention. Medical professionals later determined that Marla was in critical condition and only minutes from a fatal outcome, underscoring that the rapid response and coordinated efforts of these first responders were instrumental in saving her life; and,

WHEREAS, the lifesaving outcome of this incident reflects the extraordinary collaboration between a vigilant citizen who refused to ignore the warning signs and the dedicated first responders who acted with urgency, professionalism, and courage in the performance of their duties, demonstrating the profound impact of teamwork in a moment of crisis; and,

..title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby recognize Darcia Ashley-Amber Reed for her extraordinary vigilance, compassion, and unwavering advocacy; and, 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Tuesday, August 4, 2026 to be "Darcia Ashley-Amber Reed Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare August 22, 2026 to be “Vera Mae Williams Threet Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..body
WHEREAS, Vera Mae Williams Threet was born on August 22, 1941 to the late Ernest and Nellie Williams Sr. in Bessemer, Alabama, before her family relocated to Pittsburgh where she attended school at Fifth Ave High School and later completed her studies at the Community College of Allegheny County; and, 

WHEREAS, Mrs. Threet was an active member of Ebenezer Baptist Church where she faithfully served on the Usher Board and the Trustee Board, while also beginning her professional career with the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania as a case worker, moving on to the Pittsburgh Board of Public Education, joining the staff at Central Medical Pavilion Hospital, and concluding her career at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center; and,

WHEREAS, her service extended to the Mosiwidael Temple #1138, where she previously served as Loyal Daughter Ruler of Alpha Council #1, and was also a lifetime member and Past Grand Daughter Ruler of the National Council, as well as a longtime Trustee of the Pennsylvania State Association; and,

WHEREAS, as the ninth of twelve children in her family, which included six sisters and five brothers, Mrs. Threet is survived by her sisters Cornelia Williams and Anna Byrd, her four children with husband Raymond U. Threet Sr, Jeanette Williams, Nathaniel Williams Sr., Carmela Williams-Reese and Raymond Threet, step-children Raymond Threet, Jr., Phyllis Threet and Elizabeth Threet, nine grandchildren and eight grandchildren; and,

WHEREAS, Mrs. Threet was a proud member of the Speed Queens Women's Softball Team, where she was inducted into their Hall of Fame, and also served her community as Judge of Elections, as a member of the AARP, and as an active participant with the Black Political Empowerment Project; and,

WHEREAS, known for her warm hospitality and delicious southern cooking that brought family and friends together, Mrs. Threet was a pillar of the community that inspired those who knew and loved her;

..title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare August 22, 2026 to be "Vera Mae Williams Threet Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare July 21, 2026 to be “Yvonne F. Brown Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Body
WHEREAS, Mrs. Yvonne F. Brown has dedicated nearly eight decades to serving others, a journey defined by compassion, courage and an unwavering belief that every person deserves to be heard, respected and given an opportunity to thrive; and, 

WHEREAS, born on July 20 of 1946 to parents Carrie Wade and Harry Wade, Mrs. Brown spent the first 5 years of her life in Pittsburgh's historic hill District before moving to Penn Hills, returning to the Hill in her senior year to graduate from Fifth Ave High School in 1965; and,

WHEREAS, Mrs. Brown is the proud mother of children Anthony C. Johnson, born in 1966, Leatrice Johnson, born in 1971, Yvonne O. Brown, born in 1983, and Unique Brown, born in 1984; and,

WHEREAS, Mrs. Brown began her long and storied career working as a receptionist at Neighborhood Legal Services in 1971, while she also attended Duff's Business Institute at night, and would eventually move to California in 1976 to begin working for the Department of Human Services in Compton, California; and,

WHEREAS, returning to Pittsburgh in 1981, Mrs. Brown began working at the Hill House as a Recreation Aide under the leadership of Jim Henry, whose confidence in her advocacy helped strengthen her commitment to serving those in need; and,

WHEREAS, around 1988, Mrs. Brown began working for the Department of Public Welfare in Pittsburgh before transferring to the LIHEAP program, where she became known for treating every person with kindness and dignity, as she recognized that behind every application was a family facing difficult circumstances; and,

WHEREAS, other accomplishments at the time include attending Carlow College and volunteering at the American Red Cross, where she traveled to elementary schools in Pittsburgh's low-income neighborhoods to teach children about fire safety and emergency preparedness, and also worked with the Honorable Kathleen Mulligan; and,

WHEREAS, throughout the 1990's, Mrs. Brown witnessed several school closures in the Hill District, which prompted her to begin attending School Board meetings to speak up and advocate on behalf of Hill District children and families, and inspired the creation of her newsletter, "The Concerned Parent", to keep families informed on these issues; and,

..body
Be it resolved by the Council of the City of Pittsburgh as follows:

Section 1.	The Mayor, the Director of Public Safety and the Director of Human Resources and Civil Service, on behalf of the City of Pittsburgh, are authorized to enter into an Agreement or Agreements with the Ross and Carol Nese Foundation for the purpose of receiving grant funds in the amount not to exceed ONE MILLION ($1,000,000.00) dollars to hire a Head of Talent Acquisition, Public Safety to further the City's efforts in recruiting and retaining public safety staff. Monies from the grant agreement shall be deposited into the Grants Trust Fund account 2129400555.48311.00. 

Section 2.	The Mayor, the Director of Public Safety and the Director of Human Resources and Civil Service, on behalf of the City of Pittsburgh, are further authorized to follow regular procurement processes to make all legitimate expenditures required by said Agreement(s) as outlined in Section 1. Said grants expenditures shall not exceed ONE MILLION ($1,000,000.00) dollars chargeable to and payable from the appropriate expense account in the Grants Trust Fund, job number 2129400555.

matters.title: Ordinance amending the Pittsburgh Code of Ordinances, Title Five: Traffic, Article VII: Parking, Chapter 541: General Parking Regulations, Section 541.02: Prohibitions in Specified Places, to remove language providing an exception to parking prohibitions for the protection of a vehicle.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Title
Ordinance amending the Pittsburgh Code of Ordinances, Title Five: Traffic, Article VII: Parking, Chapter 541: General Parking Regulations, Section 541.02: Prohibitions in Specified Places, to remove language providing an exception to parking prohibitions for the protection of a vehicle.

..Body
The Council of the City of Pittsburgh hereby enacts as follows:

Section 1.  The Pittsburgh City Code, Title Five: Traffic, Article VII: Parking, Chapter 541: General Parking Regulations, Section 541.02: Prohibitions in Specified Places, is amended as follows:

� 541.02. Prohibitions in Specified Places.
Except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or to protect the safety of any person or vehicle or in compliance with law or the directions of a police officer or official traffic control device, no operator of a vehicle shall, and no owner of a vehicle shall allow the vehicle to:

(A)  Stop, stand or park a vehicle:
(1)  On the roadway side of any vehicle stopped or parked at the edge or curb of a street except that a pedalcycle may be parked as provided in Vehicle Code 3509(b)(2).
(2)  On a sidewalk except that a pedalcycle may be parked as provided in Vehicle Code 3509(b) (2).
(3)  Within an intersection.
(4)  On a crosswalk.
(5)  Between a safety zone and the adjacent curb within thirty (30) feet of points on the curb immediately opposite the ends of a safety zone, unless a different length is indicated by official traffic control devices.
(6)  Alongside or opposite any street excavation or obstruction when stopping, standing or parking would obstruct traffic.
(7)  Upon any bridge or other elevated structure upon a street or within a street tunnel.
(8)  On any railroad tracks.
(9)  In the area between roadways of a divided street, including crossovers.
(10)  At any place where official signs prohibit stopping.
(11)  In a restricted time parking zone during the posted prohibited times.
(12)  Within fifteen (15) feet of a transit stop sign.
(13)  Other than a taxicab in a taxicab stand.
(14)  To make repairs except in an emergency.
(15)  In a bicycle lane. A bicycle lane is defined as a portion of the roadway that has been designated by striping, signage, and pavement markings for the preferential or exclusive use of bicyclists.
a.   A driver of any vehicle transporting a person with a disability, which is picking up or dropping off that person(s), is exempt. Such stopping shall be limited to the time necessary to complete drop-off and/or pick

matters.textExcerpt:
..title
Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, on behalf of the City of Pittsburgh, to enter into a cooperation agreement with Allegheny County Economic Development; Allegheny County Department of Human Services; and the Urban Redevelopment Authority, to collaboratively manage coordinated entry services related to the HOME-ARP program, at no cost to the City.

..body
WHEREAS, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development ("HUD") has awarded the City $8,354,476-Eight Million, Three Hundred Fifty-Four Thousand, Four Hundred Seventy-Six Dollars, in HOME Investment Partnership Program - American Rescue Plan ("HOME-ARP") funds for fiscal year 2021; and
 
WHEREAS, the City, the Urban Redevelopment Authority, and Allegheny County Economic Development have co-invested in a variety of HOME-ARP affordable housing projects ("the Projects"); and

WHEREAS, Allegheny County Department of Human Services operates the Coordinated Entry system for the County Continuum of Care; and 

WHEREAS, Coordinated Entry requirements for HOME-ARP funded units has additional requirements above and beyond current standards; and
 
WHEREAS, the City of Pittsburgh, Allegheny County Department of Human Services, Allegheny County Economic Development, and the Urban Redevelopment Authority wish to cooperate on processes related to the Projects; and 
 
WHEREAS, the City of Pittsburgh, Allegheny County Department of Human Services, Allegheny County Economic Development, and the Urban Redevelopment Authority wish to enter into a cooperation agreement in order to memorialize respective responsibilities toward the Projects.


Be it resolved by the Council of the City of Pittsburgh as follows:

Section 1.	The Mayor and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, on behalf of the City of Pittsburgh, are hereby authorized to enter into a cooperative agreement with: Allegheny County Economic Development; Allegheny County Department of Human Services; and the Urban Redevelopment Authority, to collaboratively manage coordinated entry services related to the HOME-ARP program, at no cost to the City.

Finally, that any Ordinance or Resolution or part thereof conflicting with the provisions of this Resolution, is hereby repealed so far as the same affects this Resolution.

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Tuesday, July 21st, to be “Anthony Ceoffe Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Body
WHEREAS, Anthony Ceoffe is the Senior Director of Asset Management for the Housing Authority of the City of Pittsburgh (HACP), and, after dedicating 15 years to public service with HACP, will be transitioning into a new opportunity; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony's leadership in overseeing one of Pennsylvania's largest affordable housing portfolios has strengthened property operations, resident services, and organizational effectiveness; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony has built meaningful partnerships among neighborhood organizations, public agencies, and elected officials to strengthen Pittsburgh neighborhoods; and,

WHEREAS, included in those partnerships is collaborating to establish a working relationship between Caliguiri Plaza residents and Hilltop Community organizations, helping to create a foundation of trust and mutual respect among residents and community partners; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony is also a problem-solver who supported the Fresh Start Program in Glen Hazel, a program which prevented the displacement of dozens of families; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony's ability to build relationships, listen to residents, and create partnerships among various stakeholders has had a lasting impact on HACP communities. His ability to connect people, find common ground, and move initiatives forward has been one of his greatest strengths during his time with HACP; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony is a life-long resident of Lawrenceville who has followed the legacy of his grandparents, Anthony and Maryann Ceoffe, and his father, the Honorable District Judge Tony Ceoffe, to be an active, engaged resident in his community; and,

WHEREAS, Anthony is as devoted to his family as his work, including his daughters Gabriella and Avellina; and,

WHEREAS, Pittsburgh City Council wishes Anthony well as he will continue his commitment to community development and affordable housing in his transition to Senior Director of Property Operations with Trek Development Group;

..Title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Tuesday, July 21st, to be "Anthony Ceoffe Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare August 23, 2026 "Karla Boos Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..body
WHEREAS, Ms. Karla Boos grew up in Wheeling, West Virginia, graduated from the University of Pittsburgh, and went on to earn her Master of Fine Arts degree from the California Institute for the Arts; and

WHEREAS, Ms. Boos founded Quantum Theatre in 1990 to bring a version of the experimental theater she brought to life during her time in Los Angeles to the City of Pittsburgh's art ecosystem; and
 
WHEREAS, Quantum Theatre's first production was a low-budget staging of Harold Pinter's "The Collection" at The Artery, then a gallery and music venue in Shadyside that is now the home of the restaurant Soba; and

WHEREAS, during its early years Quantum Theatre produced one or two shows a season, many of which were staged at the old Pittsburgh Center for the Arts now known as the Pittsburgh Center For Arts & Media; and

WHEREAS, by 1997 Quantum Theatre had solidified its unique approach to environmental theater by creating new, enthralling, and unusual spaces for many productions; and

WHEREAS, Quantum Theatre stages its productions environmentally, bringing the works out of the typical theatre setting and into a variety of locations such as the One Oxford Centre in Downtown Pittsburgh, the swimming pool under Braddock Library, the Historic Carrie Blast Furnace Site, the Pittsburgh Zoo, abandoned buildings in Lawrenceville, and Mellon Park, to name a few, in an effort to transport the viewer, the staff, and the thespian to a unique environment that further enhances the company's fantastic theatrical experience while providing an appreciation for the location in question; and

WHEREAS, Karla Boos has produced all 106 of Quantum Theatre's works, directed 33, acted in 17, and wrote or adapted nine original productions of Quantum's 26 world premieres; and

WHEREAS, Quantum Theatre has become a fixture of Pittsburgh's art scene and has been recognized nationally and internationally for its innovative work; and
 
WHEREAS, Karla Boos is a member of the National Theatre Conference, the international Women's Forum, the recipient of the Carol R. Brown Award for Established Artist as well as its predecessor the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust's Creative Achievement Award for Emerging Artist; and
 
WHEREAS, the Theatre continues to support young playwrights, actors, and directors from the region and around the world; and

matters.title:
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby commend “Serbian National Federation (SNF)” in celebrating their 125th Anniversary; and, 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Saturday July, 18, 2026 to be “Serbian National Federation Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Body
WHEREAS, founded in 1901 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, the Serbian National Federation (SNF) stands as one of the oldest and most influential Serbian American fraternal organizations in the United States. Emerging during a period of heavy immigration from the Balkans, the SNF provided Serbian newcomers with a sense of stability, cultural continuity, and mutual support. Its mission-preserving Serbian heritage while empowering Serbian Americans-has guided its work for more than a century; and, 

WHEREAS, a cornerstone of the SNF's identity is its newspaper, Srbobran, first published in 1906. Created as a unifying voice for Serbian immigrants, Srbobran offered news from the homeland, updates on Serbian communities across America, and commentary on cultural and political issues relevant to the diaspora. Over time, it evolved into one of the longest running Serbian language publications in North America, serving as both a historical record and a cultural lifeline for generations; and, 

WHEREAS, education has always been central to the SNF's mission. Through its scholarship program started in 1989, it has awarded over $150,000 annually to Serbian American students pursuing higher education. These annual scholarships ease financial burdens and reinforce the SNF's commitment to developing future leaders who remain connected to their heritage; and, 

WHEREAS, community involvement remains one of the SNF's most visible strengths. The Federation sponsors cultural festivals, church events, youth programs, and humanitarian initiatives that support both Serbian Americans and communities in Serbia. Its outreach fosters unity, preserves traditions, and strengthens intergenerational ties; and,

WHEREAS, sports have long played a vibrant role in SNF life. The organization hosts an annual basketball tournament which is the oldest at 86 years and going, as well as, golf, and bowling tournaments that bring together members from across the country. These events promote camaraderie, healthy competition, and a sense of belonging-values that have sustained the SNF for more than a century; and,

WHEREAS, through its publications, scholarships, cultural programs, and athletic events, the Serbian National Federation continues to serve as a pillar of Serbian American identity. Its history reflects the resilience and dedication of a community determined to preserve its heritage while contributing meaningfully to American society. Now celebrating its 125th Anniversary; and,

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare July 19th, 2026, to be Chuck “Z-boy” Zdobinski Day in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Body
WHEREAS, as a UPS Package Car Driver, Chuck served the Lawrenceville community for over 30 years; and,  
 
WHEREAS, Chuck consistently went above and beyond anyone's expectations to complete his deliveries; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck was a familiar face loved by Lawrenceville residents, businesses, and dogs; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck thought about his customers' needs before worrying about every type of inclement weather Pittsburgh could dish out that would stop anyone else from doing what he did; and, 
 
WHEREAS, on your worst of days, Chuck would arrive with something and bring a smile to your face; and,  
 
WHEREAS, Chuck, in his "UPS Browns" was like the "Pied Piper" for every dog in the Lawrenceville neighborhood, as they would chase him for treats and 'pets'; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck treated every customer with respect and dignity; and, 
 
WHEREAS, no matter how busy Chuck's day was or how full his package car was, he took the time for even just a quick moment of pleasant conversation with anyone who wanted to talk with him; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck would always give you a honk of the horn if he saw you on the street; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck had 9,420 days worked, 2,307,900 packages delivered, 565,200 miles driven; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck went above and beyond service, as he played a part in making Lawrenceville what it is today-a thriving, welcoming community; and, 
 
WHEREAS, Chuck will be missed beyond any stretch of the imagination and there is no replacing Chuck - someone can fill his space, but no one can take his place.

..Title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare July 19th, 2026, to be Chuck "Z-boy" Zdobinski Day in the City of Pittsburgh.

matters.textExcerpt:
..title
Ordinance amending and supplementing the Pittsburgh Code of Ordinances, Title Nine, Zoning Code, Article V, Use Regulations, Chapter 911, Primary Uses, Section 911.04, Use Standards, Subsection A.41(b)(6), Multi-Suite Residential (General) in the UC-E District, is hereby amended to add a new Subsection, A.41(b)(6)(c).

..body
The Council of the City of Pittsburgh hereby enacts as follows:

Section 1.	The Pittsburgh Code, Title Nine, Zoning Code, Article V, Use Regulations, Chapter 911, Primary Uses, Section 911.04, Use Standards, Subsection A.41(b)(6), Multi-Suite Residential (General) in the UC-E District, is hereby amended and supplemented to add a new Subsection A.41(b)(6)(c) as underlined as follows (Subsection A.41(b)(6) shall remain unchanged except as underlined): 
  
(6)	In the UC-E District, Multi-Suite Residential uses shall meet one (1) of the following standards in the UC-E District: 
  
(a)	All residential units shall meet the requirements of Section 907.04.A.6 and shall otherwise follow the processes and procedures of Section 907.04.A, excluding Section 907.04.A.5 Applicability and Section 907.04.A.7 Off-Site Inclusionary Standards. One hundred (100) percent of the units shall be affordable and shall be located on site; or 
  
(b)	Residential housing shall be less than fifty (50) percent of the Gross Floor Area in a mixed-use structure. For purposes of this calculation, shared spaces between residential uses and commercial shall be excluded from the calculation of Gross Floor Area.; or 
  
(c)	For any zoning lot in the UC-E that is wholly or partially within 100 feet of an EMI District, 50-100% of the Gross Floor Area may be multi-suite residential provided the rooms are rented on a monthly basis or longer.

Section 2.	Acknowledgement.  It is hereby acknowledged that, as of the date of the passage of this ordinance, there are three (3) UC-E District areas (as such term is used in Section 1 of this ordinance), two (2) of which share at least one (1) district boundary line with the EMI District, as depicted on the exhibit attached to this ordinance. 

Section 3.	Repealer.  All ordinances and parts of ordinances inconsistent with the terms of this ordinance are hereby repealed; provided, however, that such repeals shall be only to the extent of such inconsistence and in all other aspects, this ordinance shall be cumulative of the other ordinance regulating and governing the subject matter by this ordinance.

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare July 1, 2026 to be “Younger Brothers Bar Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..Body
WHEREAS, for 20 years, Young Brothers Bar has been a staple of the Marshall Shadeland neighborhood and the broader Northside community, as a place that brings people together and celebrates the culture, history and spirit of the Northside; and, 

WHEREAS, brothers Jamie and Keith Younger, together with their father Keith Younger Sr., became successful entrepreneurs by creating a space where people from across the Northside can network and build relationships, welcoming everyone from hardworking neighbors to elected officials, in the process becoming a household name in the community; and,

WHEREAS, over the years, Young Brothers Bar has hosted community engagement events, such as voter registrations and "Get Out the Vote" efforts, community health and wellness initiatives, neighborhood beautification projects, community cleanups, food giveaways, job development workshops, and community conversations focused on improving the quality of life of Northside residents; and,

WHEREAS, Jamie and Keith Younger have not only reinvested in their business, but also invested in the surrounding community, taking an active role in cleaning the Woods Run corridor and McClure Avenue, often caring for areas beyond the immediate vicinity of their establishment; and,

WHEREAS, Jamie and Keith Younger have also served as leaders within organizations such as the Northside Leadership Conference and the Marshall Shadeland Civic Association, all the while supporting emerging entrepreneurs and new businesses by sharing their knowledge, providing mentorship, and connecting them to resources that help them succeed; and,

WHEREAS, these accomplished Black entrepreneurs deserve recognition for their hard work, dedication, leadership and unwavering commitment to the community they serve, with a legacy that extends beyond their business and a community that has become better connected thank to their efforts in the last 2 decades;

..Title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare July 1, 2026 to be "Younger Brothers Bar Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.

WHEREAS, Softball has been one of the biggest influences in Chelsea's life. It has taught her discipline, perseverance, leadership, and the importance of being part of something bigger than herself. Every season has helped shape not only the player she has become, but also the person she strives to be; and,

WHEREAS, Chelsea softball journey began in April 2017 when she joined Brookline Recreational softball League. She had the chance to make new friends, learn new skills, compete and even got the honor of being the opening day representative for the Pittsburgh Pirates and experience standing on the field during that day; and, 

WHEREAS, Chelsea was selected to the All-Star Team for four consecutive seasons, from 2018 through 2021. Those years provided her with countless memories, but none was more rewarding than July 2021, when her Brookline All-Star Team captured the Mayor's Cup Championship at PNC Park. Winning a championship on the home field of the Pittsburgh Pirates is an experience she will always cherish; and, 

WHEREAS, August 2021 Chelsea transitioned to competitive fast-pitch softball by joining the South Hills Devil Dogs 12U team. During her time on the Devil Dogs her team won the May 2023 13U championship, her first fast-pitch championship and competed in the World Series in Columbus, Ohio; and,

WHEREAS, Chelsea joined the newly formed Pittsburgh Power Voltage 14U fast-pitch team. She embraced the opportunity to become one of its leaders while expanding her versatility on the field. She transitioned into playing catcher, outfield, and first base, learning the unique responsibilities each position demands. This past season has been one of her most successful. Her team had an outstanding year, we made the Championship in 5 out of the 12 tournaments they played in.  She finished with a .328 batting average while recording 28 hits, ranking fourth on the team. She drove in 24 RBIs, which ranked second on the team, and scored 25 runs, placing third. She is especially proud of leading the team with seven homeruns; and,

WHEREAS, Chelsea attends Seton LaSalle High School, where she is a Junior Achievement Student Ambassador amassing over 75 community service hours. Volunteering at the Charlie Batch Foundation for children, member of the Book Club, participated in two fall musicals, three spring drama productions, member of the school church choir, mock trial team and flag football. matters.textExcerpt:
..body
WHEREAS, Rich Hoffman is retiring after forty-one years as a City Foreman, from December 16, 1985 to July 31, 2026; and, 

WHEREAS, Rich was a foreman at the City garage for 20 years, from 1985 to 2005, before becoming a foreman in the Department of Public Works from 2005 to 2026, working at the heavy equipment division and many maintenance divisions; and,

WHEREAS, he was also during this time a Chief Steward for AFSCME Local 2037 from 2011 to 2026, and was a member of the local's city foreman contact negotiating team 4 different times; and,

WHEREAS, Rich is a resident of Highland Park and has also worked as an usher and ticket taker at PPG Paints Arena since 2004, for a total of 22 years; and,

WHEREAS, Pittsburgh City Council wishes Rich well in his retirement and thanks him for his 41 years of exemplary service to the City of Pittsburgh;

..title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare Thursday, July 30th, to be "Rich Hoffman Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.

matters.title: NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare June 30, 2026 to be “Idella L. Michaels Day” in the City of Pittsburgh.
matters.textExcerpt:
..body
WHEREAS, Ms. Idella L. Michaels, daughter of the late Dr. LH Green, the founder of Greens Temple Church, carries forth her father's tradition of dedication, faith and service to others as administrator of Greens Temple Church; and, 

WHEREAS, through her guidance and professionalism, Ms. Michaels has consistently demonstrated a strong commitment to supporting her church, its members and those who serve within the organization, as she has led with integrity, compassion and wisdom to ensure the success of the Church's numerous programs, initiatives and services; and,

WHEREAS, Ms. Michaels leadership style reflects genuine concern for the well-being and growth of others, fostering an environment where teamwork, collaboration and mutual respect are encouraged and valued, always empowering those around her; and,

WHEREAS, in addition to her service within the church, Ms. Michaels also served as a City Investigator for more than 30 years, having always demonstrated a high level of professionalism, fairness and integrity, exemplifying the values of accountability, respect and excellence that continue to define her leadership style to this day; and,

WHEREAS, for her outstanding contributions, tireless dedication and unwavering commitment to serving others, we commend Ms. Michaels for her lifelong devotion to helping others and leaving an enduring mark on countless lives, an inspiration to all who have had the privilege of knowing and working alongside her; 

..title
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the City of Pittsburgh does hereby declare June 30, 2026 to be "Idella L. Michaels Day" in the City of Pittsburgh.
